milestones.label: Consistency of analysis posed as Hilbert's second problem
milestones.work: D. Hilbert, Mathematische Probleme, ICM address 1900
milestones.description: Hilbert asks for a direct consistency proof for analysis.

evidence.claim: SEP states the 1900 address posed this as the second problem

milestones.label: Neubegruendung der Mathematik
milestones.work: D. Hilbert, Neubegruendung der Mathematik: Erste Mitteilung, 1922 (Hamburg talks July 1921)
milestones.description: The finitary programme in its mature form, from the 1921 Hamburg talks.

evidence.claim: SEP says the programme was proposed in this form only in 1921, published 1922

milestones.label: Grundzuege der theoretischen Logik
milestones.work: Hilbert and Ackermann, Grundzuege der theoretischen Logik, 1928
milestones.description: Textbook presentation of the logic used by the programme.
milestones.note: Role consolidation is a judgment; SEP only lists the work.

milestones.label: Gentzen's consistency proof for arithmetic
milestones.work: G. Gentzen, Die Widerspruchsfreiheit der reinen Zahlentheorie, Math. Ann. 112 (1936)
milestones.description: Consistency of first-order Peano arithmetic proved with transfinite induction.

evidence.claim: SEP and Wikipedia cite Math. Ann. 112

notes: Opened SEP and Wikipedia (Hilbert's program). Catalogue citation 'Axiomatisches Denken 1918' not confirmed; not used. Goedel 1931 omitted as not a development of the programme proper without further source.

milestones.label: Parallel transport on arbitrary manifolds
milestones.work: T. Levi-Civita, Nozione di parallelismo in una varieta qualunque, Rend. Circ. Mat. Palermo 42 (1917)
milestones.description: Parallel transport extended to abstract Riemannian manifolds.

evidence.claim: Wikipedia timeline cites this paper and volume

milestones.label: Schouten and Weyl generalise
milestones.description: Schouten independently, and Weyl by generalising, extend the 1917 results.

evidence.claim: Wikipedia says both did so in 1918

milestones.note: Weyl's specific title not confirmed on the page.

notes: Cartan's connections not verified (Wikipedia page does not cover them); no Cartan milestone. Catalogue date range 1917-1925 unverified.

milestones.label: Dedekind's axiomatisation of the naturals
milestones.work: R. Dedekind, Was sind und was sollen die Zahlen?, 1888
milestones.description: Dedekind gives a similar axiomatisation and proves categoricity of the second-order form.

evidence.claim: Wikipedia states Dedekind proposed it in 1888

milestones.label: Arithmetices principia
milestones.work: G. Peano, Arithmetices principia, nova methodo exposita, 1889
milestones.description: Peano publishes a simplified version in formal logical notation.

notes: Catalogue range to 1891 unverified (Peano 1891 not on page). Only Wikipedia opened.
Wikipedia Karl Pearson opened: dates Biometrika to 1901 or 1902 inconsistently; chi-squared 1900 paper title only partly given. Not confirmed enough from primary records; left empty.
Wikipedia 'Italian school of algebraic geometry' opened: school active c. 1885-1935; no specific dated works confirmed. Catalogue 1896 citations unverified; left empty.

milestones.label: Loewenheim's theorem
milestones.work: L. Loewenheim, Ueber Moeglichkeiten im Relativkalkuel, Math. Ann. 76 (1915) 447-470
milestones.description: First proof of what became the Loewenheim-Skolem theorem.

evidence.claim: Wikipedia credits the 1915 paper with the first proof; gives title and pages

notes: Skolem 1920 simplification noted by Wikipedia (citing Brady) but no title/venue confirmed; not added. Catalogue 'Logisch-kombinatorische Untersuchungen 1920' unverified.

milestones.label: Cayley's abstract finite group
milestones.work: A. Cayley, On the theory of groups, as depending on the symbolic equation theta^n=1, Phil. Mag. 1854
milestones.description: First abstract definition of a finite group.

evidence.claim: Wikipedia says the paper gives the first abstract definition of a finite group

milestones.label: Von Dyck's axiomatic abstract group
milestones.work: W. von Dyck, Gruppentheoretische Studien, Math. Ann. 1882
milestones.description: Generators and relations and the first axiomatic definition of an abstract group.

evidence.claim: Wikipedia states von Dyck was first with an axiomatic definition

milestones.note: Exact title/year of the von Dyck paper taken from catalogue, page gave 1882.

notes: Weber and Kronecker dates unverified; Schmidt 1916 unverified.
Wikipedia page opened but history section not reached; Frobenius 1896, Burnside, Schur dates unverified; left empty.

milestones.label: Takagi's existence theorem
milestones.work: T. Takagi, Ueber eine Theorie des relativ Abel'schen Zahlkoerpers, 1920
milestones.description: Existence theorem for abelian extensions known by 1920.

evidence.claim: Wikipedia: crucial Takagi existence theorem known by 1920

milestones.note: Title from catalogue; page gives only the 1920 date.

notes: Artin 1927 and Hilbert Zahlbericht not confirmed on page. Weber coined 'class field' (page, no year).

milestones.label: Heaviside develops operational calculus
milestones.work: O. Heaviside, Proc. Roy. Soc. papers 1893-1894 and Electromagnetic Theory (1893, 1899)

evidence.claim: Wikipedia: Heaviside fully developed it in 1893, citing Proc. Roy. Soc. 1893 and 1894

milestones.label: Carson and Wiener justify the method

evidence.claim: Wikipedia dates Carson and Wiener work to 1926

notes: Bromwich 1916 and Carson 1922 not on page; omitted.

milestones.label: Grundlagen der Geometrie
milestones.description: Hilbert's axioms for Euclidean geometry, using models to prove independence.

evidence.claim: Wikipedia: first edition 1899, models used for independence

notes: Later editions: 1902 English translation (Townsend) incorporates completeness axiom.

milestones.label: Brouwer's dissertation
milestones.work: L. E. J. Brouwer, Over de Grondslagen der Wiskunde, 1907
milestones.description: Dissertation on the foundations of mathematics.

milestones.label: Heyting's formal rules
milestones.work: A. Heyting, Die formalen Regeln der intuitionistischen Logik, 1930

notes: 1908 paper on excluded middle not confirmed on page; omitted.
